title: a job cancelled during an action's `git fetch` leaves `shallow.lock` in the action cache, and every later job using that action fails
body:
## Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No (Haven’t tested)

## Description

When a job is cancelled while the runner is fetching one of its actions, the runner kills `git` with `SIGKILL`. Git can't remove its lock file, so `shallow.lock` stays in that action's bare repository in the action cache. From then on, every job on that runner that uses the action fails during setup, before its first step:

```
could not fetch remote 'origin': fatal: Unable to create '/data/.cache/act/e5/8582f2…/shallow.lock': File exists.
Another git process seems to be running in this repository, or the lock file may be stale: exit status 128
```

Nothing clears it. Re-runs and new runs keep failing until someone deletes the file (or the clone) on the runner by hand. No git process was running when I checked, so the lock was stale.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Use a workflow with `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` and a job that uses an action not yet in the runner's action cache (here `golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9`).
2. Push twice in quick succession, so the first run is cancelled while the runner is still running `git fetch` for that action. Its log ends with `could not fetch remote 'origin': : signal: killed`.
3. Every later job that uses the action fails with the `shallow.lock … File exists` error above. In my case the next run hit it 2 seconds later, and it kept failing for every run until I deleted `/data/.cache/act/e5/8582f2…` by hand.

To see the second half without timing a cancellation, create `shallow.lock` inside the action's cached repository (`$HOME/.cache/act/<xx>/<hash>/`) and start a job that uses the action.

**Cause (v13.2.1)**

- [`act/common/git/git.go#L545`](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/common/git/git.go#L545) runs git with `exec.CommandContext`. When the context is cancelled, [`act/common/cmdgroup.go#L22`](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/common/cmdgroup.go#L22) sends `SIGKILL` to git's process group. Git removes its lock files on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, but it can't on `SIGKILL`.
- The cache is meant to be reused, so the stale lock outlives the job and breaks the action for every later job on the runner.

Related, but a different cause: #1663 (several runner processes sharing one cache) and the closed #1755.

## Forgejo Version

17.0.1

## Runner Version

v13.2.1 (`data.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit:13`). The relevant code is unchanged on `main` at 80c990d.

## How are you running Forgejo?

The official container image `codeberg.org/orbit/orbit:17`, with PostgreSQL 18, behind a reverse proxy, using Docker Compose.

## How are you running the Runner?

- **Image:** the official `data.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit:13` image, run with Docker Compose as `forgejo-runner daemon --config /config.yml`.
- **Docker:** jobs run on a separate `docker:29-dind` container through `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://<dind>:2375`.
- **Cache:** `HOME=/data` on a Docker volume, so the action cache is `/data/.cache/act`. `host.workdir_parent` is unset.
- **Config:** `capacity: 2`; labels `ubuntu-latest:docker://ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest` and `docker:docker://data.forgejo.org/oci/node:lts`; cache enabled (`dir: /data/cache`).
- **Runners:** a single runner process uses this cache.

## Logs

<details>
<summary>The cancelled job (run 1), killed while fetching the action</summary>

```
2026-11-11T12:45:54.1988033Z Runner <uuid> (version:v13.2.1) received task 152 of job lint, triggered by event: push
2026-11-11T12:45:54.6789467Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/actions/checkout' # ref=v7
2026-11-11T12:45:55.0593946Z   ☁️  git clone 'https://github.com/actions/setup-go' # ref=v7
2026-11-11T12:45:55.3639436Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/actions/setup-go' # ref=v7
2026-11-11T12:45:56.2168693Z   ☁️  git clone 'https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint-action' # ref=v9
2026-11-11T12:45:56.7237313Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint-action' # ref=v9
2026-11-11T12:45:57.2879415Z ⚙️ [runner]: could not fetch remote 'origin': : signal: killed
2026-11-11T12:45:57.2953834Z 🏁  Job failed
2026-11-11T12:45:57.4521950Z context canceled
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>The next job (run 2, 2 seconds later), and every job after it that used the action</summary>

```
2026-11-11T12:45:58.1870797Z Runner <uuid> (version:v13.2.1) received task 153 of job lint, triggered by event: push
2026-11-11T12:45:58.4966030Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/actions/checkout' # ref=v7
2026-11-11T12:45:58.9263407Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/actions/setup-go' # ref=v7
2026-11-11T12:45:59.3421043Z   ☁️  git fetch 'https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint-action' # ref=v9
2026-11-11T12:45:59.7883183Z ⚙️ [runner]: could not fetch remote 'origin': fatal: Unable to create '/data/.cache/act/e5/8582f25dafc105d6bbe602703a2bb24c371b9cc0cc508be6e117328537895c/shallow.lock': File exists.

Another git process seems to be running in this repository, or the lock file may be stale: exit status 128
2026-11-11T12:45:59.7953935Z 🏁  Job failed
```

The same error recurred on every run (20:26, 20:28, …) until the directory was deleted. The job's next run then passed. These logs are at the default level; I didn't have `log.level=debug` set when it happened.

</details>

## Workflow file

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref_type != 'tag' }}

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9
        with:
          version: v2.14.0
```

title: bug: host-mode runner can't execute docker:// job step
body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

Yes

### Description

Running a docker:// job step on a host-mode runner 13.2.1 fails with the error message: [runner]: failed to start container: Error response from daemon: failed to set up container networking: network WORKFLOW-e34d3e5ab76e9ffa1bc1448a6b581344 not found

In host-mode, [act/runner/step_docker.go#L158](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/runner/step_docker.go#L158) tries to use the job network returned by [act/runner/run_context.go#L482-L491](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/runner/run_context.go#L482-L491), which is "WORKFLOW-xxx" by default when `container.network` is empty, but it's never created in [act/runner/run_context.go#L765-L774](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/runner/run_context.go#L765-L774) because it's gated behind `!isHostEnv && ContainerNetworkMode == ""`.

Container and Dockerfile actions work because [act/runner/action.go#L499-L502](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/runner/action.go#L499-L502) uses Docker's "default" network when `rc.JobContainer.ManagesOwnNetworking()`.

Minimal reproduction example: https://v18.next.forgejo.org/alex/runner-docker-host-repro/src/branch/main/.forgejo/workflows/repro.yml
Test run using my self-hosted runner: https://v18.next.forgejo.org/alex/runner-docker-host-repro/actions/runs/2/jobs/0/attempt/1

### Related issues

* https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/1668 network option was ignored; the default didn't work
* https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/1587 fix workspace for Docker steps in host-mode

### Forgejo Version

https://v18.next.forgejo.org/

### Runner Version

13.2.1

### How are you running Forgejo?

https://v18.next.forgejo.org/

### How are you running the Runner?

The runner in the repro above was registered and launched using:
$ docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" -w /data code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit:13.2.1 forgejo-runner register --no-interactive --instance https://dev.next.forgejo.org --token TOKEN --name repro-host --labels host-test:host
$ docker run --rm code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit:13.2.1 forgejo-runner generate-config > config.yml
$ vim config.yml  # to set log.level:debug and log.job_level:debug
$ docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" -w /data -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock --user 0 code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit:13.2.1 forgejo-runner daemon -c /data/config.yml

title: bug:  Runner accepts successful completion after output EOF while exec is still runnin
body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

Yes

### Description

Overview
----------
Forgejo runner returns success after a command’s output stream closes, even when the container API reports that the command is still running. This resulted in a PR that was marked to merge on success to be merged, but the tests didn't run through (30 of 136 tests ran, just stopped and the job was marked as success).
 
I reproduced it with Runner v13.2.0 and v13.2.1 on next instance:

see https://v18.next.forgejo.org/nina3/forgejo-runner-premature-success-repro
 
The CI result can be found in:
 https://v18.next.forgejo.org/nina3/forgejo-runner-premature-success-repro/actions/runs/2
 
  I also added a local script in the project to reproduce it. Run: `./reproduce.sh v13.2.1`

 Runner versions affected: v13.2.0 and v13.2.1.

What happended?
-----------------------
* Command starts successfully
* Attached output stream closes with EOF
* Container API reports `Running: true, ExitCode: 0`.

What I expect
-----------
The incomplemete execution should be rejected, or it should be waited for the actual result to complete.

What actually happended
-------------------
The execturo returns `nil`, indicating a success

Possible fix (tried)
--------

When adding guard against `Running: true`, the test runs through
 
 
 Related issue
-------------
https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/1615)

title: bug: nested conditionals sometimes drops parentheses
body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No

### Description

The following 2 files together makes `callee` execute, even though it should be logically impossible. This happens because the parentheses in `needs.decide.result == 'failure' && (false || true)` gets dropped, effectively rewriting the expression to `needs.decide.result == 'failure' && false || true` where `&&` binds tighter.

```
# .forgejo/workflows/repro.yml
on: push
jobs:
  decide:
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
  call:
    needs: decide
    if: needs.decide.result == 'failure' && (false || true)
    uses: ./.forgejo/workflows/callee.yml
```

```
# .forgejo/workflows/callee.yml
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  should-be-skipped:
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
```

title: bug: The default value of a `case` expression is not properly serialized
body:

If a case expression `${{ case(cond, then, default) }}` is evaluated with a falsy condition `cond`, then the value of `default` is not properly serialized if it's not a string: in my case `default` was a number (namely the context value `forge.event.pull_request.number`), which got serialized as `"<float64-value>"`.

title: A composite action's job summary is shown twice (runner 13.2.0)
body:
### What happens

A line that a `run:` step inside a **composite action** appends to `$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY` (or
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`) appears **twice** in the job summary that Forgejo 17 shows above the job's log. The same
line written by a plain `run:` step at the top level of the job appears once.

### Versions

- forgejo-runner v13.2.0 (Linux, Docker back end; the code below is identical on `main` today)
- Forgejo v17.0.0

### Reproduce

`.forgejo/actions/summary-once/action.yml`:

```yaml
name: summary-once
description: Writes one line to the job summary
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      run: echo "- written once by the composite action" >>"$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

`.forgejo/workflows/summary.yml`:

```yaml
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  summary:
    runs-on: docker
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.forgejo/actions/summary-once
      - run: echo "- written once by a plain step" >>"$FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

**Expected:** each line once. **Actual:** "written once by the composite action" twice, "written once by a plain step"
once.

### Why (from reading v13.2.0)

- `act/runner/step.go`, `runStepExecutor`: before every step that runs it points `FORGEJO_STEP_SUMMARY` and
  `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` at `<actPath>/workflow/SUMMARY.md` and empties that file; after the step,
  `processRunnerSummaryCommand` reads the file and logs it as a `command: summary` entry. It does not empty the file
  afterwards.
- The composite action's run context shares the parent's job container (`action_composite.go`), so the inner `run:`
  step and the outer `uses:` step read **the same** `SUMMARY.md`.
- The outer `uses:` step also goes through `runStepExecutor` (`step_action_local.go` / `step_action_remote.go`), so
  after the whole action it reads the file again, which still holds the inner step's line.
- The inner step's logger keeps the outer step's number (`WithCompositeStepLogger` in `job_executor.go`), and
  `Reporter.Fire` (`internal/pkg/report/reporter.go`) and the step-summary collector append every `command: summary`
  entry under that number without de-duplication.

So the inner step's line is reported once by the inner step and once more by the outer step.

### Workaround

End the composite action with an empty step that runs on every path, for example:

```yaml
    - if: always()
      shell: bash
      run: ':'
```

Because every step that runs starts with `SUMMARY.md` emptied, the outer step's second read then finds nothing and the
line shows once. (On Windows, a `shell: powershell` step with `run: '$null'` does the same.)

### A possible fix

Either empty `SUMMARY.md` after `processRunnerSummaryCommand` has read it, or skip the summary read for a step whose
action is composite (its inner steps already report their own).

title: bug: plugin UDS authority is incompatible with many servers
body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

Yes

### Description

When connecting to a plugin over unix domain socket, the HTTP/2 `:authority` header is set to the path of the socket.
This is incompatible with several HTTP/2 server implementations including hyperium/h2 and NodeJS.
The same kind of issue was brought up in [grpc-go#2628](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/2628) and grpc-go now defaults to sending `localhost`.
Runner still has the issue because we construct a passthrough address
https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/commit/c4a92ffa5e3a400ae7e9c40a2914e649eb338ad7/act/plugin/client.go#L124-L130
removing that custom handling fixes the issue.

### Forgejo Version

v16.0.5

### Runner Version

v13.2.0

### How are you running Forgejo?

Official Docker Image

### How are you running the Runner?

linux release via command-line

### Logs

With a tonic server on the plugin side
